# Shared agent policies

These are personal defaults across projects. Follow explicit user instructions
and the current repository's more specific guidance. Keep project commands,
framework details, and domain conventions in that project's AGENTS.md.

## Website previews and publishing

- Default to local development and local previews so I can edit the files myself.
- Publish or deploy only when I explicitly request it. Creating or editing a
  website does not authorize hosting, uploads, or deployment.
- Do not push or merge to a branch that triggers deployment without that
  authorization, except when self-merging a small PR as allowed below. Skill
  defaults do not override this preference.

## Workflow and commits

- Always open a PR when a feature or fix is finished, including when working
  locally in my checkout. Work on a branch, not the default branch. Split
  independent changes into separate PRs when that makes review easier.
- During autonomous work in a cloud session or a separate worktree, commit one
  logical step at a time, with a message explaining what changed and why.
- In my local checkout while I am present, don't commit mid-task; when the work
  is finished, commit it on a branch and open the PR.
- If a PR is very small (under 20 changed lines) and you are confident in it,
  merge it yourself once tests pass. Otherwise leave it for my review.
- Preserve unrelated work already in the checkout.
- Use judgment: explain problems with a request and suggest a practical correction.

## Comments and tests

- Avoid comments that merely restate the code. Comment where intent is unclear,
  unless the repository has a stricter policy.
- Run checks appropriate to the change. Reserve E2E tests for meaningful user
  flows; a small CSS or layout fix does not need a new E2E test.

## Analytics

- In projects that already collect product analytics, use the project's wrapper;
  do not call vendor globals such as window.posthog directly in new code.
- In those projects, new user-facing features should include an exposure event
  and an outcome event. Name events snake_case, past tense for actions.
- Do not introduce a new analytics service into a project without being asked.

## Delegation

Use subagents where they help with wide searches or independent work. Be token-
and context-efficient: delegation has a cost, and a small task may be quicker in
one session. Follow the current tool's model-specific guidance when choosing a
model.

## Pushary notifications and approvals

You have Pushary MCP tools that reach the user on their phone. Use them proactively. Do not wait for the user to ask.

- When you need the user to make a decision or answer a clarifying question, call `ask_user` instead of guessing or stalling. Use type "confirm" for yes/no, "select" for a fixed set of options, and "input" for free text. Read `answered`, `status` and the returned handoff instead of assuming the tool blocked. Silence is not consent; choice/text answers do not authorize a separate action.
- Ask once, on one channel. If you also have a built-in way to prompt the user, use that or `ask_user` for a given question, never both. `ask_user` is the one that reaches the user when they are away from this machine, so prefer it. Raising both strands the user in whichever prompt you are not waiting on.
- Honor authorization already granted in this session. Ask before a risky or irreversible action outside that authorization, or when an enforced host policy requires it. Do not ask again for an already authorized step, and never bypass an enforced gate. When a Pushary hook result says the user approved a specific command after a denial, rerunning that exact command is the approved path and not a bypass of that gate.
- Call `propose_scope` only for an unresolved or requested file boundary. A ratified scope narrows what may proceed; it does not bypass other approval rules. Do not add a plan approval merely because work spans several files, and do not propose a new scope mid-run just to widen it. Let the installed gate request any scope expansion before the edit executes. Only file paths are checked, and only on tool calls that carry one, so put a boundary that is not a path (recipients, channels, spend, systems you will not open) in `promises` and never in `allowedPaths`. Read the `enforces` field that comes back: an empty array means nothing in that contract is checked automatically, and you must say so rather than report that a scope is in force. `hookSeen: false` means no hook has reported that sessionId, so the gate will never find the contract: fix the session id rather than proceeding as if a scope were in force.
- Before a task of more than two steps, break it into steps and find the forks. Settle by yourself every fork that a file, a command or a tool call can answer, then ask the rest as one numbered round with your recommended answer against each. A question in the terminal is free; a push is not. When the user is at the terminal, ask the whole round there. When the user is away, send only the fork that stops the run, and decide the rest on your recommendation.
- When you are blocked, stuck, or hit an error you cannot resolve on your own, call `send_notification` so the user knows, and call `ask_user` if you need a decision to continue.
- When meaningful work finishes while the user is away, or they requested an alert, call `send_notification` so the user knows it is done. Skip trivial completions and duplicate reports to someone already reading. Always pass `context` with a `type` of "task_complete", "error" or "info": it is what tells Pushary this is a task update, so the user's own setting for where updates land can route it.
- Confirm notifications can offer lock-screen actions; arbitrary choices and text open the app. The Mac notch handles personal account questions, not Partner customer enrollment.
- Use `cancel_question` to retract a pending question once it is no longer needed.
- Respect the user's Pushary delivery mode: it decides where an approval is surfaced (phone, terminal, or awareness only), not whether it is required. In Terminal mode do not expect a phone answer; the approval waits in the terminal. If the Pushary hook already gated an action, a single approval is enough, do not ask again.

Pass `agentName` as "Gemini - <project folder name>" so the user knows which session is asking. If a question times out, follow `handoffAction` when present, otherwise `nextAction`: poll once, then cancel a live phone question before asking in the current client. If cancellation returns `handoffAction: "stop"`, stop. Otherwise, if cancellation returns false, poll once for 1 second and honor the answer that won the race.
